known_differences.description: CG method uses Polak-Ribiere+ formula; SciPy uses Fletcher-Reeves by default in older versions.
Ridder method available as root_scalar(method='ridder'); same convergence contract as brentq for smooth functions.

threats.description: BFGS gradient finite-difference approximation can produce catastrophic cancellation on ill-conditioned objectives near machine epsilon, leading to Hessian approximation corruption and divergent search directions.
threats.mitigation: Detect non-finite gradient estimates and terminate with NanEncountered status. In hardened mode, reject immediately with diagnostic message.
threats.strict_mode_response: Report NanEncountered convergence status with non-finite context in message.
threats.hardened_mode_response: Immediate rejection with 'hardened mode rejects non-finite objective values' message.

threats.description: Flat or near-flat objective landscapes (e.g., quartic near origin) can cause BFGS/CG to consume function evaluation budget without meaningful progress, effectively creating a compute denial-of-service.
threats.mitigation: Enforce strict maxfev budget. Terminate with MaxEvaluations status when budget is exhausted regardless of gradient state.
threats.strict_mode_response: Terminate and report MaxEvaluations with evaluation count in message.
threats.hardened_mode_response: Same as strict; budget enforcement is unconditional.

threats.description: Bracket endpoints that do not satisfy the sign-change invariant (f(a)*f(b) < 0) will cause bracketing methods to silently compute incorrect results or enter infinite loops if not validated upfront.
threats.mitigation: Validate bracket sign change before entering iteration loop. Return immediate error with diagnostic message.
threats.strict_mode_response: Error: 'bracketing methods require f(a) and f(b) to have opposite signs'.
threats.hardened_mode_response: Same error with additional context about hardened rejection policy.

threats.description: Root functions that return NaN or Inf at evaluation points corrupt the bracketing interval state, potentially causing the algorithm to converge to a non-root or diverge.
threats.mitigation: Check every function evaluation for finiteness. In strict mode, return error immediately. In hardened mode, reject with explicit policy message.
threats.hardened_mode_response: Error: 'hardened mode rejects non-finite function values'.

threats.description: Extremely tight tolerance requirements (e.g., xtol=1e-18) with low maxiter budgets will prevent convergence, potentially leaving the user with an interval that does not contain the root to desired precision.
threats.mitigation: Track convergence status explicitly. Return MaxIterations status with the best estimate when budget is exhausted, so callers can distinguish budget exhaustion from other failures.
threats.strict_mode_response: Return unconverged result with MaxIterations status and iteration count.
threats.hardened_mode_response: Same behavior; budget enforcement is unconditional.

threats.description: Empty or zero-length x0 vectors bypass dimension-dependent default parameter calculations (maxiter, maxfev), and can cause division by zero or index-out-of-bounds in algorithm internals.
threats.mitigation: Validate x0 non-emptiness and finiteness before entering any optimization algorithm.
threats.strict_mode_response: Error: 'x0 must be a finite 1-D vector with at least one element'.
threats.hardened_mode_response: Same error; input validation is unconditional.

threats.description: Zero or negative xtol values can prevent convergence detection, as the interval width check (|b-a| < xtol) would never be satisfied or always be satisfied.
threats.mitigation: Validate xtol > 0 before entering iteration loop.
threats.hardened_mode_response: Same error; parameter validation is unconditional.
